newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil Tiger rebels bombard Sri Lankan troops.
newsitem.headline: Tamil Tiger rebels bombard Sri Lankan troops.

text.p: Sri Lankan Tamil Tiger guerrillas shelled government troops on the eastern flank of a two-pronged thrust by the military into rebel territory, armed forces officials said on Thursday.

Three soldiers were wounded and a 12-year-old boy was killed overnight during the artillery bombardment in and around Weli Oya, a remote Sinhalese settlement some 250 km (156 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo, they said.

Weli Oya was one of the launch pads for the army's current offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", in which troops backed by tanks, artillery and air cover drove deep into rebel-held areas in this island's northern Wanni region.

Two army divisions are moving on separate flanks in what military analysts say is an attempt to cut through rebel-held areas to ensure that the guerrillas are thinly spread on the ground and unable to launch a concerted attack.

Troops pushed north from bases in northeastern Weli Oya and northern Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, last week in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The military now relies on costly and tenuous air and sea links to supply bases and civilians in Jaffna.

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, control vast swathes of land in the mostly shrub-covered Wanni between Jaffna and Vavuniya.
One army division that broke out from Weli Oya, on the eastern flank of the offensive, captured Nedunkeni, about 40 miles (25 km) northeast of Vavuniya.
The other division, advancing from Vavuniya, seized Omanthai, nine miles (14 km) north of the town on the road to Jaffna.
Both units were poised to push further into rebel territory once they consolidate positions in newly captured areas and bring up reinforcements.
According to Defence Ministry figures, 67 soldiers have been killed and 96 wounded in the offensive. But hospital sources said some 320 soldiers had been wounded.
The ministry says rebel radio transmissions intercepted by the army indicated 181 Tigers had been killed and 316 wounded in the fighting. It said the dead included several rebel leaders.
The LTTE have accused the military of killing Tamil civilians and destroying property under the pretext of opening a supply route, and of routinely exaggerating rebel casualties.

Aid workers have said food was running low in the Wanni, where civilians have been displaced by the offensive. They said in Vavuniya that no food convoys had gone north since the army offensive began last Tuesday.
But the military has denied there is a food shortage, saying enough stocks were sent before the offensive began.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the civil war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
